BVD clinical characteristics — DR Congo

At a glance

current selection
Analytic scope: records that reached sample collection / testing (a sample, laboratory record or final classification); never-sampled / invalidated alerts are excluded. Two status axes are used throughout. Test status = laboratory-confirmed vs test-negative vs unknown (sampled but not yet classified). Vital outcome = died (recorded as a death alert or deceased at sample collection) vs no death recorded — the latter does not imply survival (outcome may simply be unrecorded), so death proportions are not a case-fatality rate. The time window is anchored on notification date.

How often is each field filled in?recorded vs missing
How to read these analyses. Figures describe associations in observational data — they do not prove cause and effect. Confidence intervals are not adjusted for looking at many symptoms at once, so treat single ‘significant’ cells cautiously and favour overall patterns. Right truncation and incomplete follow-up matter especially for recent weeks and for onset-based delays (see Methods for technical detail).

no individual timelines

Aggregated view of healthcare workers in the current selection (counts, age/sex mix, top symptoms, recorded deaths). Fine-grained timelines and onset dates are not shown, to reduce re-identification risk when numbers are small.

3 · Mortality by admission date

deaths / admissions per week

Weekly proportion of admitted individuals recorded as having died, by week of hospital admission (Wilson 95% CI), with weekly admission volume for context.

Interpretation caveat. Recent weeks often look artificially ‘low mortality’ because deaths (and hospital exits) are recorded with lag — incomplete follow-up, not necessarily improving survival. Compare earlier weeks for more stable proportions.

4 · Signs & symptoms at presentation — confirmed vs negative

Table 1

Relative difference in presenting signs and symptoms between laboratory-confirmed and test-negative case-patients (records with a completed symptom field). Risk difference uses a Newcombe 95% CI; risk ratio a Katz-log 95% CI (computed live for the current selection). Green = lower in confirmed, red = higher in confirmed.

Interpretation caveats. Both groups are suspected BVD patients who met the symptom-based case definition, so absolute frequencies are inflated and the confirmed-vs-negative contrast may be attenuated by symptoms shared through the case definition. This is a screen over ~20 symptoms with no multiplicity adjustment: at 95% confidence, roughly one comparison in twenty is expected to exclude the null by chance, so read the overall pattern rather than individual coloured cells.

5 · Confirmed symptoms & association with death

prevalence + death RR

Left: how common each presenting symptom is among laboratory-confirmed cases. Right: relative risk of a recorded death among confirmed cases who present with each symptom versus those who do not.

Clinical triage. Identifying patients at higher risk of death supports decisions such as closer observation and more intensive nursing. These panels summarise associations in the line list; they do not replace bedside assessment.

Left: pairwise correlation (φ coefficient) between presenting symptoms. Right: an UpSet plot of the most frequent combinations of the six most common symptoms. Both default to confirmed cases; switch cohort at right.

Clinical reading (6b). Frequent combinations that include diarrhoea, vomiting or haemorrhagic signs suggest many patients are already in the ‘wet’ symptomatic phase at presentation — relevant for isolation, PPE and triage.

7 · Ct values by vital outcome

Altona (PCRA) · ante-mortem blood

Cycle-threshold (Ct) values among confirmed positives, by vital outcome, for the Altona (PCRA) assay. Restricted to ante-mortem blood specimens: deceased-at-collection samples are almost entirely post-mortem swabs (a different specimen with degraded RNA), so an unrestricted died-vs-alive Ct comparison would confound outcome with specimen type. Lower Ct = higher viral load; the caption gives median [IQR] and the crude difference (small ante-mortem death counts, so interpret cautiously). Ct is not comparable across assays.

Altona (PCRA), HEX target

Onset documentation — included vs excluded

selection check for onset-based analyses

The delay distributions (§8–10) condition on a reliable symptom onset (≥ 15 Jun 2026) and are complete-case — a minority of confirmed cases. This table compares those that qualify with those excluded (standardized differences) so any selection bias is visible.

empirical + epidist / MLE fits

Empirical delay histograms with parametric fits adjusting for double interval-censoring and right truncation.

Ct control & assay separation. For onset→admission, Ct strata are split at the within-assay median and reported separately for RADIONE and Altona, since Ct is not comparable across assays/locations. Where a stratum has too few records for a stable fit, only the empirical distribution is shown.

11 · Admission delay vs symptoms at onset

median onset→admission

Whether presenting with a given symptom at onset is associated with a faster or slower onset→hospital-admission delay.

Interpretation caveat. Self-reported symptom onset is often imprecise. Patterns such as severe signs (e.g. haemorrhage) appearing to start only one or two days before admission are clinically unexpected and usually mean the onset date is unreliable — treat these delay estimates with low confidence.

Supplementary · signs & symptoms among the deceased

positive vs negative · died only

Table 4 restricted to individuals recorded as having died — comparing presenting signs and symptoms of confirmed-positive vs test-negative fatal cases (same estimators as Table 4). Sample sizes are smaller, so several risk ratios may be imprecise or not estimable.

Supplementary · age- & sex-adjusted symptom associations

modified Poisson · confirmed cases

Adjusted risk ratios (mirrors Table S1) for each presenting symptom among confirmed cases, from modified Poisson regression (log link, robust variance) with male sex and age (per 10-yr increment) entered simultaneously. Precomputed for the selected time window. NE = not estimable (<10 events or <3 in a sex stratum).

Method & symptom-code note. These are exploratory analyses without prespecified multiplicity adjustment: confidence-interval widths are not adjusted for multiplicity and should not be used in place of hypothesis testing. Symptom codes follow Symptoms_en.csv; three French codes were inferred and flagged with *: DT=Chest pain, DRO=Retro-orbital pain, ICT=Jaundice.
